## Motivation

`_cuda_host_register` (HiCache host pools, mamba/DSA/MHA host buffers) and `_cuda_host_unregister_ranges` (their teardown) format a failed CUDA call with `cudart.cudaGetErrorString(rc)` after converting the return value to `int`. torch's binding (`torch.cuda.cudart()`) returns `cudaError` values, and its `cudaGetErrorString` accepts only those:

```
TypeError: cudaGetErrorString(): incompatible function arguments. The following argument types are supported:
    1. (arg0: torch._C._cudart.cudaError) -> str
```

So the error path raises a `TypeError` instead of the intended message, and the actual CUDA error (e.g. `part or all of the requested memory range is already mapped`) is lost. In teardown, an unregistration failure that should be logged as a warning raises instead. The existing unit tests use a fake runtime that takes ints, so they could not catch this.

## Modifications

- `mem_cache/pool_host/common.py`: keep the `cudaError` value returned by `cudaHostRegister` / `cudaHostUnregister`, compare `int(err)`, and pass the value itself to `cudaGetErrorString`. Messages, return values and control flow are otherwise unchanged.
- New `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_cuda_host_register_errors.py` (`base-b`, `1-gpu-small`, skipped without CUDA). It triggers real CUDA errors through torch's binding:
  - registering the same buffer twice must raise `RuntimeError("cudaHostRegister failed (rc=..., <CUDA error text>) ...")`;
  - unregistering a range that was never registered must be logged as a warning with the CUDA error text, and returned as a failed range.
  - after each forced failure, a torch kernel launch consumes the leftover CUDA error, so later tests in the same process are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: error-reporting code only; success paths are unchanged.

## Reproduction and Regression Tests

Same GPU (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), same `lmsysorg/sglang` nightly image (torch 2.14.1+cu130), upstream main vs this branch:

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_cuda_host_register_errors.py` (new) | `FAILED (errors=2)`: `TypeError: cudaGetErrorString(): incompatible function arguments` | `Ran 2 tests ... OK` |
| `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_host_register.py` | 15 OK | 15 OK |
| `test/registered/hicache/test_dsa_host_release.py` | 1 passed | 1 passed |
| `test/registered/hicache/test_k_only_host_release.py` | 1 passed | 1 passed |
| `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py` | 176 passed | 176 passed |
| `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_minimax_m31_cache_transfer.py` | 35 passed | 35 passed |
| `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_minimax_sparse_pool_pd_unit.py` | 4 OK | 4 OK |
| `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/` (whole directory in one pytest process, without the 2-GPU `test_page_interleave_gather_multi_gpu.py`; 1x H100) | 3630 passed, 27 failed, 13 errors | 3632 passed, 27 failed, 13 errors (same failing tests as main) |

With the fix, the new test checks that the raised `RuntimeError` carries the CUDA error text (it matches `cudaHostRegister failed \(rc=\d+, [^)]*already`), and that the unregister failure is logged with it rather than raised. `test_unified_hicache_transfer_lifecycle.py` errors identically on main and here (4 of 8, its Rust extension is not built in the image), so it is left out of the table.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no change on the success path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`pre-commit run --all-files` clean)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (fails on main with the TypeError, passes here)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing change)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (not applicable: error path only)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -179,11 +179,13 @@ def _cuda_host_register(
         while offset < total:
             size = min(chunk_bytes, total - offset)
             ptr = base + offset
-            rc = int(cudart.cudaHostRegister(ptr, size, 0))
+            # Keep the cudaError value: cudaGetErrorString does not take an int.
+            err = cudart.cudaHostRegister(ptr, size, 0)
+            rc = int(err)
             if rc != 0:
                 raise RuntimeError(
                     f"cudaHostRegister failed (rc={rc}, "
-                    f"{cudart.cudaGetErrorString(rc)}) at offset={offset} size={size} "
+                    f"{cudart.cudaGetErrorString(err)}) at offset={offset} size={size} "
                     f"(total={total}, chunk_limit={chunk_bytes}); host buffer is not "
                     f"pinned and device transfers may silently return stale data."
                 )
@@ -210,14 +212,15 @@ def _cuda_host_unregister_ranges(
 ) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
     failed_ranges = []
     for ptr, size in reversed(registered_ranges):
-        rc = int(cudart.cudaHostUnregister(ptr))
+        err = cudart.cudaHostUnregister(ptr)
+        rc = int(err)
         if rc != 0:
             failed_ranges.append((ptr, size))
             logger.warning(
                 "cudaHostUnregister failed during %s (rc=%d, %s) for ptr=%#x size=%d",
                 operation,
                 rc,
-                cudart.cudaGetErrorString(rc),
+                cudart.cudaGetErrorString(err),
                 ptr,
                 size,
             )

@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+"""CUDA errors from host-memory registration reach the caller with their text.
+
+torch.cuda.cudart() returns cudaError values, and its cudaGetErrorString only
+accepts those, so formatting the message from an int raised a TypeError that
+replaced the CUDA error. These tests trigger real CUDA errors through torch's
+binding (the fake runtime in test_hicache_host_register.py takes ints).
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.common import (
+    _cuda_host_register,
+    _cuda_host_unregister,
+    _cuda_host_unregister_ranges,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+
+def _clear_cuda_error() -> None:
+    # The forced failures leave a CUDA error that the next kernel-launch check
+    # in this process would report, failing an unrelated test. Let a torch
+    # launch check consume it, then check that the next launch succeeds.
+    try:
+        torch.zeros(1, device="cuda")
+    except RuntimeError:
+        pass
+    torch.zeros(1, device="cuda")
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.version.cuda is not None,
+    "needs the CUDA runtime",
+)
+class TestCudaHostRegisterErrors(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        torch.cuda.init()
+
+    def test_registration_error_names_the_cuda_error(self):
+        buffer = torch.empty(1 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        _cuda_host_register(buffer)
+        self.addCleanup(_cuda_host_unregister, buffer)
+        # Registering the same range twice is a real CUDA error.
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
+            RuntimeError, r"cudaHostRegister failed \(rc=\d+, [^)]*already"
+        ):
+            _cuda_host_register(buffer)
+        _clear_cuda_error()
+
+    def test_unregister_error_is_logged_with_the_cuda_error(self):
+        buffer = torch.empty(4096, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        ranges = [(buffer.data_ptr(), 4096)]
+        with self.assertLogs(
+            "sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.common", level="WARNING"
+        ) as logs:
+            failed = _cuda_host_unregister_ranges(
+                torch.cuda.cudart(), ranges, operation="test"
+            )
+        _clear_cuda_error()
+        self.assertEqual(failed, ranges)
+        self.assertRegex(
+            logs.output[0], r"cudaHostUnregister failed during test \(rc=\d+, \w"
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
